enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Normal operation

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Any error causes the HALT bit to set. Subsequently, all service requests are ignored until the HALT bit is cleared.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Normal operation

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Stall the start of any new channels. Executing channels are allowed to complete. Channel execution resumes when this bit is cleared.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Channel linking is disabled for all channels.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Channel linking is available and controlled by each channel's link settings.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Master ID replication is disabled for all channels.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Master ID replication is available and is controlled by each channel's CHn_SBR[EMI] setting.

enumeratedValue.name: IDLE
enumeratedValue.description: eDMA is idle.

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: eDMA is executing a channel.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: No destination bus error

enumeratedValue.name: ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: The last recorded error was a bus error on a destination write

enumeratedValue.name: NO_ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: No source bus error

enumeratedValue.name: ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: The last recorded error was a bus error on a source read

enumeratedValue.name: NO_ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: No scatter/gather configuration error

enumeratedValue.name: ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: The last recorded error was a configuration error detected in the TCDn_DLASTSGA field. This field is checked at the beginning of a scatter/gather operation after major loop completion if TCDn_CSR[ESG] is enabled. TCDn_DLASTSGA is not on a 32 byte boundary.

enumeratedValue.name: ERROR

enumeratedValue.description: No destination offset configuration error

enumeratedValue.name: ERROR

enumeratedValue.name: NO_ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: No destination address configuration error

enumeratedValue.name: ERROR

enumeratedValue.name: NO_ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: No source offset configuration error

enumeratedValue.name: ERROR

enumeratedValue.name: NO_ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: No source address configuration error.

enumeratedValue.name: ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: The last recorded error was a configuration error detected in the TCDn_SADDR field. TCDn_SADDR is inconsistent with TCDn_ATTR[SSIZE].

enumeratedValue.name: NO_ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: No canceled transfers

enumeratedValue.name: ERROR

enumeratedValue.name: PRE_ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: ADC analog circuits are pre-enabled and ready to execute conversions without startup delays (at the cost of higher DC current consumption). Note that a single power up delay (CFG[PUDLY]) is executed immediately once PWREN is set, and any detected trigger does not begin ADC operation until the power up delay time has passed. After this initial delay expires the analog remains pre-enabled and no additional delays are executed.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: FAULTx CPU interrupt requests disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: FAULTx CPU interrupt requests enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: NORMAL
enumeratedValue.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).

enumeratedValue.name: SAFE
enumeratedValue.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.

enumeratedValue.name: MANUAL
enumeratedValue.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].

enumeratedValue.name: AUTOMATIC
enumeratedValue.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.

enumeratedValue.description: Count up.

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTDOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Count down.

enumeratedValue.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER
enumeratedValue.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and then continue by re-initializing the counter from the LOAD register.

enumeratedValue.name: UNTIL_COMPARE
enumeratedValue.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.

enumeratedValue.name: REPEAT
enumeratedValue.description: Count repeatedly.

enumeratedValue.name: UNTIL_COMPARE
enumeratedValue.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTUP
enumeratedValue.description: Count up.

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTDOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Count down.

enumeratedValue.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER
enumeratedValue.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and then continue by re-initializing the counter from the LOAD register.

enumeratedValue.name: UNTIL_COMPARE
enumeratedValue.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.

enumeratedValue.name: REPEAT
enumeratedValue.description: Count repeatedly.

enumeratedValue.name: UNTIL_COMPARE
enumeratedValue.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.

enumeratedValue.description: Outer-set values are ready to be loaded into inner-set and take effect. The loading time point depends on CTRL2[LDMOD].

enumeratedValue.name: DMAEN_0
enumeratedValue.description: DMA is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: DMAEN_1
enumeratedValue.description: DMA is enabled. DMA request asserts automatically when the values in the outer-set of buffered compare registers (UCOMP0/LCOMP0;UCOMP1/LCOMP1;UCOMP2/LCOMP2;UCOMP3/LCOMP3), initial registers(UINIT/LINIT) and modulus registers (UMOD/LMOD) are loaded into the inner-set of buffer and then LDOK is cleared automatically. After the completion of this DMA transfer, LDOK is set automatically, it ensures outer-set values can be loaded into inner-set which in turn triggers DMA again.

field.name: HNE
field.description: Use Negative Edge of HOME/ENABLE Input

enumeratedValue.name: HNE0
enumeratedValue.description: When CTRL[OPMODE] = 0,use HOME positive edge to trigger initialization of position counters. When CTRL[OPMODE] = 1,use ENABLE high level to enable POS/POSD/WDG/REV counters

enumeratedValue.name: HNE1
enumeratedValue.description: When CTRL[OPMODE] = 0,use HOME negative edge to trigger initialization of position counters. When CTRL[OPMODE] = 1,use ENABLE low level to enable POS/POSD/WDG/REV counters

field.name: HIP

enumeratedValue.description: No action

enumeratedValue.name: HIP1
enumeratedValue.description: HOME signal initializes the position counter

enumeratedValue.description: Disabled

enumeratedValue.name: HIE1
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled

enumeratedValue.description: No transition on the HOME/ENABLE signal has occurred

enumeratedValue.name: HIRQ1
enumeratedValue.description: A transition on the HOME/ENABLE signal has occurred

enumeratedValue.name: OPMODE0
enumeratedValue.description: Decode Mode: Input nodes INDEX/PRESET and HOME/ENABLE are assigned to function of INDEX and HOME.

enumeratedValue.name: OPMODE1
enumeratedValue.description: Count Mode: Input nodes INDEX/PRESET and HOME/ENABLE are assigned to functions of PRESET and ENABLE. In this mode: (1)only when ENABLE=1, all counters (position/position difference/revolution/watchdog) can run, when ENABLE=0, all counters (position/position difference/revolution/watchdog) can't run. (2) the rising edge of PRESET input can initialize position/revolution/watchdog counters (position counter initialization also need referring to bit CTRL[REV]).

enumeratedValue.name: LDMOD0
enumeratedValue.description: Buffered registers are loaded and take effect immediately upon CTRL[LDOK] is set.

enumeratedValue.name: LDMOD1
enumeratedValue.description: Buffered registers are loaded and take effect at the next roll-over or roll-under if CTRL[LDOK] is set.

enumeratedValue.name: REVMOD0
enumeratedValue.description: Use INDEX pulse to increment/decrement revolution counter (REV)

enumeratedValue.name: REVMOD1
enumeratedValue.description: Use modulus counting roll-over/under to increment/decrement revolution counter (REV)

enumeratedValue.name: OUTCTL0

enumeratedValue.name: OUTCTL1
enumeratedValue.description: All POS_MATCH[x](x range is 0-3) are asserted a pulse, when the UPOS, LPOS, REV, or POSD registers are read

enumeratedValue.name: PMEN0
enumeratedValue.description: Period measurement functions are not used. POSD is loaded to POSDH and then cleared whenever POSD, UPOS, LPOS or REV is read.

enumeratedValue.name: PMEN1
enumeratedValue.description: Period measurement functions are used. POSD is loaded into POSDH and then cleared only when POSD is read.

enumeratedValue.name: INT_NOCLEAR
enumeratedValue.description: Do not clear the interrupt.

enumeratedValue.description: Clear the IF field (interrupt flag).

enumeratedValue.description: No interrupt is pending.

enumeratedValue.name: INT_NOPEND
enumeratedValue.description: An interrupt is pending.

enumeratedValue.description: Disable interrupts to the system.

enumeratedValue.name: EN_INT
enumeratedValue.description: Enable interrupts to the system.

enumeratedValue.description: Compatible with BC1.1 (default)

enumeratedValue.name: BC12
enumeratedValue.description: Compatible with BC1.2

enumeratedValue.name: NO_START
enumeratedValue.description: Do not start the sequence. Writes of this value have no effect.

enumeratedValue.name: START
enumeratedValue.description: Initiate the charger detection sequence. If the sequence is already running, writes of this value have no effect.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_RESET
enumeratedValue.description: Do not perform a software reset.

enumeratedValue.name: SW_RESET
enumeratedValue.description: Perform a software reset.

field.name: CLOCK_UNIT

enumeratedValue.name: MHZ_CLK
enumeratedValue.description: MHz Speed (between 1 MHz and 1023 MHz)

field.name: CLOCK_SPEED
field.description: Numerical Value of Clock Speed in Binary

enumeratedValue.name: NO_RESULT
enumeratedValue.description: No results to report.

enumeratedValue.name: CONN_SDP
enumeratedValue.description: Attached to an SDP. Must comply with USB 2.0 by drawing only 2.5 mA (max) until connected.

enumeratedValue.name: CONN_CP
enumeratedValue.description: Attached to a charging port. The exact meaning depends on the STATUS[SEQ_STAT] field (value 0: Attached to either a CDP or a DCP. The charger type detection has not completed. value 1: Attached to a CDP. The charger type detection has completed.)

enumeratedValue.name: CONN_DCP
enumeratedValue.description: Attached to a DCP.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_DATA_PIN_CONN
enumeratedValue.description: The module is either not enabled, or the module is enabled but the data pins have not yet been detected.

enumeratedValue.name: DATA_PIN_CONN
enumeratedValue.description: Data pin contact detection is complete.

enumeratedValue.name: CP_DET_DONE
enumeratedValue.description: Charging port detection is complete.

enumeratedValue.name: CT_DET_DONE
enumeratedValue.description: Charger type detection is complete.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_SEQ_ERR
enumeratedValue.description: No sequence errors.

enumeratedValue.name: SEQ_ERR
enumeratedValue.description: Error in the detection sequence.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_TIMEOUT
enumeratedValue.description: The detection sequence is not running for over 1 s.

enumeratedValue.name: TIMEOUT
enumeratedValue.description: It is over 1 s since the data pin contact was detected and debounced.

enumeratedValue.name: SEQ_NOT_RUNNING
enumeratedValue.description: The sequence is not running.

enumeratedValue.name: SEQ_RUNNING
enumeratedValue.description: The sequence is running.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_OVERRIDE
enumeratedValue.description: No overrides. Field must remain at this value during normal USB data communication to prevent unexpected conditions on USB_DP and USB_DM pins. (Default)

enumeratedValue.name: PRI_DET_OVERRIDE
enumeratedValue.description: Enables VDP_SRC voltage source for the USB_DP pin and IDM_SINK current source for the USB_DM pin.

field.name: OM1
field.description: Output Compare Operating Mode for Channel 1

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Output disabled. No response on the signal.

enumeratedValue.name: TOGGLE
enumeratedValue.description: Toggle output

enumeratedValue.name: CLEAR
enumeratedValue.description: Clear output

enumeratedValue.name: SET
enumeratedValue.description: Set output

enumeratedValue.name: PULSE
enumeratedValue.description: Generate a low pulse that is one input clock cycle wide on the output signal. When OMn is first programmed as 1xx, the output is set to one immediately on the next input clock (if it was not already). The input clock here refers to the clock selected by the CLKSRC field of this register.

enumeratedValue.name: isf0
enumeratedValue.description: Configured interrupt is not detected.

enumeratedValue.description: Configured interrupt is detected. If the pin is configured to generate a DMA request, then the corresponding flag will be cleared automatically at the completion of the requested DMA transfer. Otherwise, the flag remains set until a logic 1 is written to the flag. If the pin is configured for a level sensitive interrupt and the pin remains asserted, then the flag is set again immediately after it is cleared.

enumeratedValue.name: isf1
enumeratedValue.description: Configured interrupt is detected on the pin of the same number. If the pin is configured to generate a DMA request, then the corresponding flag will be cleared automatically at the completion of the requested DMA transfer. Otherwise, the flag remains set until a logic 1 is written to the flag. If the pin is configured for a level sensitive interrupt and the pin remains asserted, then the flag is set again immediately after it is cleared.

field.name: FGM
field.description: Legacy RX FIFO Global Mask Bits

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Disable

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Enable

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: EXT
field.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR

field.name: EXT
field.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: EXT
field.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: PRIO

field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR

field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: PRIO

field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: EXT
field.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: EXT
field.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.name: EXT
field.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

enumeratedValue.name: TRIG1
enumeratedValue.description: Write 1 to trigger power switch off

field.name: RST_CTRL_SOFT
field.description: Software reset control. This field can only be updated while LPM_MODE=0.

enumeratedValue.name: TRIG0
enumeratedValue.description: Clear to 0 to trigger reset deassert

enumeratedValue.name: TRIG1
enumeratedValue.description: Write 1 to trigger reset assert

field.name: ISO_ON_SOFT
field.description: Software isolation on control. This field can only be updated while LPM_MODE=0.

enumeratedValue.name: TRIG0
enumeratedValue.description: Clear to 0 to trigger isolation off

enumeratedValue.name: TRIG1
enumeratedValue.description: Write 1 to trigger isolation on

field.name: EDGELOCK_HDSK_SOFT
field.description: Software Edgelock handshake control. This field can only be updated while LPM_MODE=0.

enumeratedValue.name: TRIG0
enumeratedValue.description: Clear to 0 to trigger Edgelock handshake for power on.

enumeratedValue.name: TRIG1
enumeratedValue.description: Write to 1 to trigger Edgelock handshake for power off.

field.name: PDN_SOFT
field.description: By flow sequence, Software power down sequence includes Edgelock handshake for power down, isolation on, reset assert, power off; Software power up sequence includes power up, reset deassert, isolation off, Edgelock handshake for power up. This bit can only be updated while LPM_MODE=0.

enumeratedValue.name: TRIG0
enumeratedValue.description: Clear to 0 to trigger a power up sequence.

enumeratedValue.name: TRIG1
enumeratedValue.description: Write 1 to trigger a power down sequence.

field.name: PON_CNT_MODE
field.description: Configures the acknowledge counter for power up working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field

enumeratedValue.name: VAL0
enumeratedValue.description: Not use counter, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC once get Edgelock ack

enumeratedValue.name: VAL1
enumeratedValue.description: Delay after receiving Edgelock ack, delay cycle number is PON_CNT_CFG

enumeratedValue.name: VAL2
enumeratedValue.description: Ignore Edgelock ack, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when counting to PON_CNT_CFG value

enumeratedValue.name: VAL3
enumeratedValue.description: Time out mode, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when either Edgelock ack received or counting to PON_CNT_CFG value

field.name: POFF_CNT_MODE
field.description: Configures the acknowledge counter for power down working mode, locked by LOCK_CFG field

enumeratedValue.name: VAL0
enumeratedValue.description: Not use counter, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC once get Edgelock ack

enumeratedValue.name: VAL1
enumeratedValue.description: Delay after receiving Edgelock ack, delay cycle number is POFF_CNT_CFG

enumeratedValue.name: VAL2
enumeratedValue.description: Ignore Edgelock ack, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when counting to POFF_CNT_CFG value

enumeratedValue.name: VAL3
enumeratedValue.description: Time out mode, raise Edgelock handshake done to GPC when either Edgelock ack received or counting to POFF_CNT_CFG value

field.name: PON_ACK
field.description: Indicates this mix power up sequence has accepted Edgelock ack

enumeratedValue.name: DIS
enumeratedValue.description: Does not get Edgelock ack for power up.

enumeratedValue.name: EN
enumeratedValue.description: Gets Edgelock ack for power up.

field.name: PON_BUSY
field.description: Busy requesting Edgelock handshake for power up

enumeratedValue.name: DIS
enumeratedValue.description: Does not send Edgelock handshake for power up.

enumeratedValue.name: EN
enumeratedValue.description: Sends Edgelock handshake for power up.

field.name: POFF_ACK
field.description: Indicates this mix power down sequence has accepted Edgelock ack

enumeratedValue.name: DIS
enumeratedValue.description: Does not get Edgelock ack for power down.

enumeratedValue.name: EN
enumeratedValue.description: Gets Edgelock ack for power down.

field.name: POFF_BUSY
field.description: Busy requesting Edgelock handshake for power down

enumeratedValue.name: EN
enumeratedValue.description: Does not send Edgelock handshake for power down.

enumeratedValue.name: DIS
enumeratedValue.description: Sends Edgelock handshake for power down.

peripheral.name: IERC_F0_PCI_HDR_TYPE0
peripheral.description: PCI Express ECAM Event Collector config

register.name: PCI_CFH_DID_VID
register.description: PCI device ID and vendor ID register

field.name: VENDOR_ID
field.description: Vendor ID This field identifies the manufacturer of the device

field.name: DEVICE_ID
field.description: Device ID This field identifies the device ID of the device

field.name: INTR_DISABLE
field.description: Interrupt disable This field controls the ability of an Event Collect to assert the INTx wired interrupts

field.name: INTR_STATUS
field.description: Interrupt Status When set, indicates that an INTx interrupt is pending for the Event Collector

field.name: CAP_LIST
field.description: Capabilities List Indicates the presence of an Extended Capability list item

register.name: PCI_CFH_REVID_CLASSCODE
register.description: PCI revision ID and classcode register

field.name: REV_ID
field.description: Revision ID This register specifies a device specific revision identifier and is a vendor defined extension to the Device ID

field.name: CLASS_CODE
field.description: Class code The Class Code register is read-only and is used to identify the generic function of the device and, in some cases, a specific register level programming interface

field.name: CACHE_LINE_SIZE
field.description: Cache line size The Cache Line Size register is set by the system firmware or the operating system to system cache line size

field.name: HDR_TYPE
field.description: Header type This field identifies the layout of the second part of the predefined header (beginning at byte 10h in Configuration Space)

field.name: MULT_FUNC_DEV
field.description: Multi-function device When set, indicates that the Root Complex contains multiple Event Collectors.

field.name: SUBSYSTEM_VENDOR_ID
field.description: This read only field identifies the manufacturer of the subsystem

field.name: SUBSYSTEM_ID
field.description: This read only field identifies the particular subsystem

field.name: CAP_PTR
field.description: This register is used to point to a linked list of new capabilities implemented by this device

field.name: INT_LINE
field.description: Interrupt Line register communicates interrupt line routing information

field.name: INT_PIN
field.description: The Interrupt Pin register is a read-only register that identifies the legacy interrupt Message(s) the function uses

field.name: CAP_ID
field.description: Indicates the PCI Express Capability structure. Hardwired to 10h.

field.name: NEXT_CAP_ID
field.description: This field contains the offset to the next PCI Capability structure or 00h if no other items exist in the linked list of capabilities

field.name: CAP_VER
field.description: Capability Version Indicates PCI-SIG defined PCI Express Capability structure version number

field.name: DEV_PORT_TYPE
field.description: Device/Port type Indicates the specific type of this PCI Express Function

field.name: INT_MSG_NUM
field.description: Interrupt message number This field indicates which MSI/MSI-X vector is used for the interrupt message generated in association with any of the status bits of this capability structure

field.name: FLR_CAP
field.description: Function level reset capability This bit applies to Endpoints only, hardwired to 0b.

field.name: TRANS_PEND
field.description: Transaction pending When set, this bit indicates that the Event Collector has issued Non-Posted Requests that have not been completed

field.name: PME_INT_EN
field.description: PME interrupt enable When Set, this bit enables PME interrupt generation upon receipt of a PME Message as reflected in the PME Status bit

field.name: PME_REQ_ID
field.description: PME requester ID This field indicates the PCI Requester ID of the last PME Requester

field.name: PME_STATUS
field.description: PME status This bit indicates that PME was asserted by the PME Requester indicated in the PME Requester ID field

field.name: PME_PEND
field.description: PME pending This bit indicates that another PME is pending when the PME Status bit is Set

field.name: CAP_ID
field.description: Indicates the PCI-PM Capability structure. Hardwired to 01h.

field.name: NEXT_CAP_ID
field.description: This field contains the offset to the next PCI Capability structure or 00h if no other items exist in the linked list of capabilities

field.name: VERSION
field.description: Version RCEC complies with the PCI PM specification, rev 1.2.

field.name: PME_SUPPORT
field.description: PME support Event Collector does not support generating PM_PME notifications, hardwired to 00h.

register.name: PCI_CFC_PCIPM_CTL_STAT
register.description: PCI PCI-PM control and status register

field.name: PWR_STATE
field.description: Power state This field is used to set and report the power state of a function as follows: 00b = D0 01b = D1 (not supported by EC) 10b = D2 (not supported by EC) 11b = D3 If, for any reason, the operating system software attempts to put a function into a power management state that the function does not support, the function should handle this gracefully and remain in whatever state it was in before the request

field.name: NO_SOFT_RST
field.description: No soft reset When set ("1"), this bit indicates that when RCEC transitions from D3hot to D0active because of modifying Power State bits in the PCI_CFC_PCIPM_CTL_STAT register, no internal reset is issued and Configuration Context is preserved

field.name: PCIE_EXT_CAP_ID
field.description: The Extended Capability ID for the AER Extended Capability is 0001h.

field.name: CAP_VER
field.description: Capability version Must be 1h for this version of the specification.

field.name: NEXT_CAP_OFF
field.description: Next capability offset This field contains the offset to the next PCI Express Capability structure or 000h if no other items exist in the linked list of capabilities

register.name: PCIE_CFC_AER_ROOT_ERR_CMD
register.description: PCIe AER root error command register

field.name: CORR_ERR_RPT_EN
field.description: Correctable error reporting enable When set, this bit enables the generation of an interrupt when a correctable error is reported by any of the Integrated Endpoints (iEPs) or the Event Collector itself

field.name: NON_FATAL_ERR_RPT_EN
field.description: Non-fatal error reporting enable When set, this bit enables the generation of an interrupt when a non-fatal error is reported by any of the Integrated Endpoints (iEPs) or the Event Collector itself

field.name: FATAL_ERR_RPT_EN
field.description: Fatal error reporting enable When set, this bit enables the generation of an interrupt when a fatal error is reported by any of the Integrated Endpoints (iEPs) or the Event Collector itself

register.name: PCIE_CFC_AER_ROOT_ERR_STAT
register.description: PCIe AER root error status register

field.name: ERR_CORR
field.description: Correctable error received Set when a correctable error message is received and this bit is not already set

field.name: MULT_ERR_CORR
field.description: Multiple correctable errors received Set when a correctable error message is received and ERR_CORR received is already set

field.name: ERR_FATAL_NON_FATAL
field.description: Fatal/Non-fatal error received Set when either a fatal or a non-fatal error message is received and this bit is not already set

field.name: MULT_ERR_FATAL_NON_FATAL
field.description: Multiple fatal/non-fatal errors received Set when either a fatal or a non-fatal error is received and ERR_FATAL_NON_FATAL received is already set

field.name: FIRST_UCORR_FATAL
field.description: First uncorrectable error fatal Set when the first uncorrectable error message received is for a fatal error

field.name: ERR_NON_FATAL
field.description: Non-fatal error received Set when one or more non-fatal uncorrectable error messages have been received

field.name: ERR_FATAL
field.description: Fatal error received Set when one or more fatal uncorrectable error messages have been received

register.name: PCIE_CFC_AER_ERR_SRC_ID
register.description: PCIe AER error source identification register

field.name: ERR_CORR_SRC_ID
field.description: ERR_CORR Source Identification Loaded with the Requester ID indicated in the received ERR_CORR message when the ERR_CORR received bit is not already set

field.name: ERR_FATAL_NON_FATAL_SRC_ID
field.description: ERR_FATAL_NON_FATAL Source Identification Loaded with the Requester ID indicated in the received ERR_FATAL_NON_FATAL message when the ERR_FATAL_NON_FATAL received bit is not already set

register.name: PCIE_CFC_RCEC_EPA_EXT_CAP_HDR
register.description: PCIe RCEC Endpoint association extended capability header

field.name: PCIE_EXT_CAP_ID
field.description: The Extended Capability ID for the Event Collector Endpoint Association Capability is 0007h.

field.name: CAP_VER
field.description: Capability version Must be 1h for this version of the specification.

field.name: NEXT_CAP_OFF
field.description: Next capability offset This field contains the offset to the next PCI Express Capability structure or 000h if no other items exist in the linked list of capabilities

register.name: PCIE_CFC_RCEC_EPA_BITMAP
register.description: PCIe RCEC Endpoint association bitmap registerr

peripheral.name: IERC_IERB
peripheral.description: Event Collector Integrated Endpoint Register Block

register.name: F0_EC_CFH_DIDVID
register.description: Function 0 EC config header device ID and vendor ID register

field.name: VENDOR_ID
field.description: Vendor ID This field identifies the manufacturer of the device as shown in the PCIe Vendor ID Register (00h)

field.name: DEVICE_ID
field.description: Device ID This field identifies the device ID of the device shown in the PCIe Device ID Register (02h)

register.name: F0_EC_CFH_SIDSVID
register.description: Function 0 EC config header subsystem ID and subsystem vendor ID register

field.name: SUBSYSTEM_VENDOR_ID
field.description: Subsystem Vendor ID This field identifies the manufacturer of the subsystem as shown in the PCIe Subsystem Vendor ID Register (2Ch)

field.name: SUBSYSTEM_DEVICE_ID
field.description: Subsystem Device ID This field identifies the particular subsystem as shown in the PCIe Subsystem ID Register (2Eh)

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTER_DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: counter disabled

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTER_ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: counter enabled

enumeratedValue.name: INTERRUPT_DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: counting down to 0 does not assert the SysTick exception request

enumeratedValue.name: INTERRUPT_ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: counting down to 0 asserts the SysTick exception request

enumeratedValue.name: EXTERNAL_CLOCK
enumeratedValue.description: external clock

enumeratedValue.name: PROCESSOR_CLOCK
enumeratedValue.description: processor clock

field.name: COUNTFLAG
field.description: Returns 1 if timer counted to 0 since the last read of this register.

field.name: RELOAD
field.description: Value to load into the SysTick Current Value Register when the counter reaches 0

field.name: CURRENT
field.description: Reads current counter value at the time the register is accessed. Any write to the register clears the register to 0.

field.name: TENMS
field.description: Reload value to use for 10ms timing

field.name: SKEW
field.description: Indicates whether the TENMS value is exact

enumeratedValue.name: EXACT_VALUE
enumeratedValue.description: 10ms calibration value is exact

enumeratedValue.name: INEXACT_VALUE
enumeratedValue.description: 10ms calibration value is inexact, because of the clock frequency

field.name: NOREF
field.description: Indicates whether the device provides an alternative reference clock

enumeratedValue.name: CLOCK_PROVIDED
enumeratedValue.description: The alternative reference clock is provided

enumeratedValue.name: CLOCK_DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: The alternative reference clock is not provided
